newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 25.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The stock market continued Monday's fall during trading on Tuesday with the PX50 dropping 1.2 percent. Traders expect the trend to be a short-term price correction and that the market will rise beginning next week.
- IPB a.s's plan to release global depositary receipts may be in jeopardy according to economic experts.
- Skoda Plzen a.s. may found three joint ventures with China for manufacturing lorries and heavy machinery, according to the Chinese Engineering Minister.

- Further privatisation of Komercni Banka a.s., Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. and Ceska Sporitelna a.s. should resume next year. The chairman of the National Property Fund, Roman Ceska, stated that the privatisation will continue once the banking sector is more stable.
- Health insurance companies owe pharmacies an average of 500 thousand crowns per pharmacy, down from 700 thousand crowns last year.
- The Vitkovice steel company expects to obtain an important contract to supply coal-mining equipment to China. The contract should be worth tens of millions of dollars.

- Trinecke Zelezarny, which was forced to reduce plant production due to a damaging flood at the begininng of September, has said that damages directly relating to the flood amount to three million crowns while indirect damage amounts to 2.5 million crowns.
- Interkontakt, the largest Czech trading group, posted turnover of 6.1 billion crowns in the first half of 1996. This is an increase of 33 percent over the same period a year earlier.
- OMV Ceska Republkika, a daughter company of Austria's OMV AG, is expecting significant increases in competition among fuel companies in the near future.
PRAVO - The Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, Jindrich Vodicka, is planning to introduce major changes to the retirement insurance system.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus publicly admitted yesterday that large, partially state-owned banks are to some extent to blame for Agrobanka's crisis.
- The budget for the Ministry of Agriculture will increase by 12 percent in 1997 to 15.720 billion crowns from this year's 14.036 billion crowns .
- Leasing of automobiles in the Czech Republic is essentially divided between three firms, Skofin, CAC Leasing and IMP Leas.
